summary: Refine the accepted all-degree character-sheaf plan by indexing effective away-divisor choices on the native weighted divisor carrier, extending fibre tensor lines and translation to signed divisors, specifying uniqueness relative to all normalization maps, and pulling multiplication to the entire root-section space. Import all thirteen existing GC.5 targets unchanged by id. Geometric descent, lisse operations and missing Lean carriers remain explicit supplier leaves; this is a complete planning pass, not a claim that the sheaf theory is built.

nodes.title: Admissible auxiliary divisor index
nodes.statement: For fields k,F with a k-algebra structure on F, S a set of places, and integers d,B, define auxiliaryDivisors(S,d,B) as the set of native TauCeti divisors D with 0<=D coefficientwise, D(P)=0 for every P in S, and B<=d+degree(D). Degree is the residue-degree-weighted homomorphism at the pin. Under the point-place dictionary for the curve, take S to be the places of R; this is exactly the effective away-divisor choice set in the parent auxiliary-divisors target.
hypotheses: The native definition needs only Field k, Field F, Algebra k F. Nonemptiness additionally assumes IsFunctionField k F and an explicit place P outside S; no residue-degree-one condition. The geometric comparison uses X as in the conventions and the degree-preserving point-place dictionary.
proofSteps: Use TauCeti.Divisor and its coefficientwise order; impose the three conditions as a subset without choosing a divisor or a rational point.
The API is projection of these conditions. For addition use degree_add and degree_nonneg on an effective summand; coefficientwise D<=D+E and E<=D+E follow from effectivity.
For the nonempty API use the pinned exists_le_degree_add_nsmul_ofPoint on the zero divisor with bound B-d and the given away place. The resulting n times [P] is effective and vanishes at S.
Transport the set through AlgebraicCurves Layer 12A/12D, not through an invented closed-point carrier; the parent auxiliary-divisors theorem supplies an away closed point on the nonempty open U.
acceptance: Equality of native and geometric choice conditions must preserve residue degrees, effectivity and ramification support.
For an away degree-two place, d=-5 and B=3, four copies are admissible and three are not.
For two members D,E the member D+E is a common upper bound. A signed negative prime is never a member.

sources.locator: Appendix A.2.2, pp. 521–522; Lemma A.10, p. 522
sources.match: The translated construction needs effective away divisors crossing a lower bound; admissibility imposes a lower bound rather than equality of degree.

nodes.title: Signed divisor tensor line
nodes.statement: Extend the parent effective divisorTensorLine to the free abelian group Div(U). For D=sum_x n_x[x] with n_x in Z, tensor, for each closed x, all conjugate geometric stalk lines of L over x, each to power n_x (negative power means dual), with the cyclic Frobenius permutation and local action. Equivalently for D=A-C with A,C effective away from R, set Lambda_D=Lambda_A tensor Lambda_C^dual. The effective sum comparison induces canonical decomposition-independent identifications and a symmetric monoidal functor to the groupoid of one-dimensional Qbar_ell vector spaces with continuous k-Galois action. Its value agrees with the parent effective line for effective D; no ordering or chosen geometric lift belongs to the data.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g; R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, rho=deg R, U=X minus R.

ell is a prime different from char(k); coefficients are Qbar_ell. The input L is an arbitrary rank-one lisse local system on the square-root curve X_1^sqrtR, with its k-descent. Inertia over R has order dividing two; global monodromy is not assumed quadratic.

Use the actual root Picard stack P^d of triples (M,K_R,i:K_R tensor K_R isomorphic to M restricted to R), and the parent unshifted symmetric local systems L_n and high-degree descents H_n for n at least B=rho+max(2g-1,1). All sheaf maps are Frobenius-equivariant.
proofSteps: Use the parent effective divisor line and sum comparison, whose coherence is inherited from GC.3 symmetric multiplicativity, associativity and symmetry.

Define the negative factors by actual duals of rank-one Frobenius lines. For A-C=Aprime-Cprime, use A+Cprime=Aprime+C and the effective sum comparison, then tensor-cancel the C,Cprime factors. Coherence gives independence of intermediate decomposition.
Check zero, addition, inverse and symmetry on a common effective refinement. Geometric conjugate permutations supply descent at a nonrational closed point; the dual inverts that action.
The necessary lisse tensor/dual carriers and coherence are the inherited GC.3 supplier gap, not new coherent-module theory.
acceptance: The construction is independent of expressing a divisor as a difference of effective divisors.
At -[x] with degree(x)=2 the line is the dual of both conjugate fibres together, with inverse cyclic Frobenius action.
Lambda_D tensor Lambda_-D cancels canonically to the unit, also for nonquadratic L.

sources.locator: Appendix A.2.2, end of p. 521 and p. 522, immediately before (A.7)

nodes.title: Universal property of normalized character presentations
nodes.statement: Fix d in Z and the geometric conventions. For every effective admissible D let Q_D=t_D^*H_(d+degD) tensor Lambda_D^dual. Write c_DE:Q_D isomorphic to Q_E for the parent canonical comparisons and q_D:Q_D isomorphic to P_d for their canonical identifications with the parent all-degree character. They satisfy q_E composed with c_DE=q_D. For any actual lisse sheaf M on P^d, precomposition with all q_D gives a bijection from Hom(P_d,M) to families f_D:Q_D to M satisfying f_E composed with c_DE=f_D for every D,E. Consequently any lisse sheaf equipped with compatible isomorphisms from all Q_D has a unique isomorphism from P_d respecting every normalization. This uniqueness includes the comparison data, not the bare underlying sheaf.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g; R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, rho=deg R, U=X minus R.

ell is a prime different from char(k); coefficients are Qbar_ell. The input L is an arbitrary rank-one lisse local system on the square-root curve X_1^sqrtR, with its k-descent. Inertia over R has order dividing two; global monodromy is not assumed quadratic.

Use the actual root Picard stack P^d of triples (M,K_R,i:K_R tensor K_R isomorphic to M restricted to R), and the parent unshifted symmetric local systems L_n and high-degree descents H_n for n at least B=rho+max(2g-1,1). All sheaf maps are Frobenius-equivariant.
proofSteps: Use the nonempty effective choice set from the parent auxiliary-divisors theorem; use the parent choice-comparison and choice-cocycle to obtain q_D and its compatibility.
Choose one admissible D0 only for the proof. For a compatible family set f=f_D0 composed with q_D0 inverse. The cocycle identity shows f composed with q_D=f_D for every D.
The same identity proves independence of D0; since q_D0 is an isomorphism it also proves uniqueness. Apply the result to isomorphism families for the final uniqueness statement.
This is a consequence of the normalization construction in A.2.2, not an additional descent theorem or an assertion that arbitrary Picard sheaves are classified by divisor values.
acceptance: A scalar twist of q_D0 at one choice and no others is not a compatible family unless the scalar is 1.
For high d, use the admissible zero divisor and recover the original high-degree descent H_d with its pullback comparison.
At d=-1 use any sufficiently large multiple of an away closed point; the uniqueness proof never requires a degree-one divisor.

sources.locator: Appendix A.2.2, pp. 521–522, comparison of choices before Lemma A.10
sources.match: Canonical identification of every normalized presentation implies this compatible-morphism universal property. The bijection is a derived API statement, not a separately numbered theorem in the paper.

nodes.title: Coherent signed character translation
nodes.statement: For d in Z and any signed divisor D supported on U, let delta_D be its canonical root Picard k-point given by O_X(D), with the trivial root over R determined by the rational section there; put t_D(M)=M tensor delta_D. There is a canonical Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism theta_(d,D):t_D^*P_(d+degD) isomorphic to P_d tensor Lambda_D, where P_d is the parent all-degree character and Lambda_D is the signed line. It agrees with the parent effective translation when D>=0. With t_E composed with t_D=t_(D+E), theta_(d,D+E) equals the composite t_D^*theta_(d+degD,E) followed by theta_(d,D) tensor id and Lambda_D tensor Lambda_E identified with Lambda_(D+E). The zero comparison is the identity and the D,-D composite is the identity after evaluation. These equalities are taken with the specified Picard and sheaf associators, not on trace functions alone.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g; R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, rho=deg R, U=X minus R.

ell is a prime different from char(k); coefficients are Qbar_ell. The input L is an arbitrary rank-one lisse local system on the square-root curve X_1^sqrtR, with its k-descent. Inertia over R has order dividing two; global monodromy is not assumed quadratic.

Use the actual root Picard stack P^d of triples (M,K_R,i:K_R tensor K_R isomorphic to M restricted to R), and the parent unshifted symmetric local systems L_n and high-degree descents H_n for n at least B=rho+max(2g-1,1). All sheaf maps are Frobenius-equivariant.
proofSteps: Use parent effective-pullback to identify delta_A^*P_(degA) with Lambda_A for effective A. Parent multiplication and unit give the corresponding value at the inverse delta_C, and identify delta_D^*P_(degD) with Lambda_A tensor Lambda_C^dual for D=A-C.
The signed line decomposition API proves independence of A,C. Restrict parent mu_(d,degD) along id times delta_D to obtain theta_(d,D).
Restrict parent character-associativity to id times delta_D times delta_E to prove composition. Restrict parent symmetry-unit to get zero and the inverse law, using signed-line evaluation.

Agreement with the effective translation is checked after further effective high-degree translation and the normalized universal property. No map adding a negative divisor to an effective symmetric power is introduced.
acceptance: For d=-1 and D=-[x] at an away degree-two point, the map is t_-x^*P_-3 isomorphic to P_-1 tensor Lambda_x^dual.
Composing D and -D returns P_d with its identity, rather than a scalar multiple.
For an effective D both definitions of translation coincide as sheaf maps; order-three Frobenius is inverted for negative D.

sources.locator: Appendix A.2.2, pp. 521–522, signed translation reduction and (A.7); Proposition A.11, pp. 522–523
sources.match: Signed divisor translation is used in the all-degree construction. Restricting the character multiplication makes its identity, composition and inverse compatibility explicit.

nodes.title: Character comparison on the full section space
nodes.statement: For d,e>=0 let hatX_d be the parent whole root-section space, hatAJ_d its forgetful map and hatL_d=hatAJ_d^*P_d on all of hatX_d. Pulling parent mu_(d,e) through the square hatAJ_(d+e) composed with hatadd_(d,e)=mult composed with (hatAJ_d times hatAJ_e) gives a canonical isomorphism hatadd_(d,e)^*hatL_(d+e) isomorphic to hatL_d external-tensor hatL_e. The isomorphisms obey associativity, symmetry and the unit diagrams for the effective empty-section object. On the effective opens they are the parent symmetric multiplication alpha_(d,e). At every geometric pair of objects, including either or both global sections equal to zero, this remains an isomorphism of rank-one stalks. No extension by zero from the effective open is used.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g; R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, rho=deg R, U=X minus R.

ell is a prime different from char(k); coefficients are Qbar_ell. The input L is an arbitrary rank-one lisse local system on the square-root curve X_1^sqrtR, with its k-descent. Inertia over R has order dividing two; global monodromy is not assumed quadratic.

Use the actual root Picard stack P^d of triples (M,K_R,i:K_R tensor K_R isomorphic to M restricted to R), and the parent unshifted symmetric local systems L_n and high-degree descents H_n for n at least B=rho+max(2g-1,1). All sheaf maps are Frobenius-equivariant.

Only the parent source-defined d,e>=0 section spaces and their actual addition maps enter this target. The effective empty divisor has global section 1; the zero global section is not the tensor unit.
proofSteps: Use the GC.1 root-addition and root-abel-jacobi square on the entire section spaces, including zero sections.
Apply inverse image to parent all-degree-multiplication and the inverse-image/external-tensor comparison of the actual lisse category.

Pull parent associativity and symmetry-unit through the triple and swapped squares. On effective opens, full faithfulness of the high-degree comparison and the parent effective-pullback identify this map with alpha; arbitrary effective degrees follow by the common-normalization cocycle.

For geometric zero-section points the underlying Picard object remains defined; pullback of its rank-one line has rank one. This is the whole-space object used in the published consumer, not a new compact-support construction.
acceptance: At a degree-d zero global section and an effective degree-e point the output global section is zero but its stalk is P_at_M tensor P_at_N, a nonzero line.
Restriction to the effective product recovers alpha_(d,e) including d=e=0.
The effective empty divisor is the unit. The degree-zero zero-section object is a different section object, although its underlying Picard point can be the unit.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1.4–A.1.5, p. 517; Lemma A.8, pp. 520–521; Proposition A.11, pp. 522–523
sources.match: Tensoring section data commutes with forgetting to the root Picard stack; pulling character multiplication through that square gives the whole-space comparison.

sources.match: The consumer takes inverse image of the character sheaf on the entire hat space. Its specialization to the quadratic-cover input supplies the motivating example, without restricting the general Appendix A input to quadratic monodromy.
